issues.title: Phase1 ~1.5B follow-up: free Render runtime restarts at LLAMA_START
issues.body:
## Actual execution finding on 2026-10-03

Frozen TCC `PHASE1_MVP_TCC_V1` authorized exactly one ~1.5B follow-up because the valid schema-constrained 0.5B assay collapsed (modal share 1.0, family accuracy 0.10).

### Fixed assay
No prompt/fixture/grammar/temperature/scoring change was made.
- model family: Qwen2.5 Instruct
- candidate: `bartowski/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-GGUF`
- file: `Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf`
- expected SHA-256: `1adf0b11065d8ad2e8123ea110d1ec956dab4ab038eab665614adba04b6c3370`
- llama.cpp: `b11146`
- dataset digest: `8bfce027bdc82a34b78e9b1a87f7812d907db34c164f50a9a996bd41b3b824d6`
- execution wrapper source: commit `1726631145e91ace2aa23931fb844bb9c86d2057`
- Render free service: `srv-db01rtnavr4c73dqnv9g`

### Observed sequence
Run 1 reached:
`RUNTIME_ACQUIRE -> MODEL_ACQUIRE -> FIXTURE_GENERATE -> LLAMA_START`
and the service process restarted before `INFERENCE`.

Run 2 repeated the same sequence and again reached `LLAMA_START` before restart.

Because `FIXTURE_GENERATE` occurs only after model download and SHA verification, model acquisition/integrity passed.

### Classification
This is **not** a 1.5B model accuracy/capacity result. No fixture inference completed.

The restart occurs during llama model startup on a 512MB free Render instance. Resource pressure is strongly suspected, but no explicit OOM log was emitted, so OOM must not be claimed as proven.

### Required handling
1. Stop the restart loop.
2. Preserve the frozen assay unchanged.
3. Move only the execution/transport host: reuse the existing range-transfer path to move the already SHA-verifiable public model from Render to GPT sandbox, then execute the same assay there.
4. Do not branch to 4B automatically.
5. Do not record `CAPACITY_LIMIT_AFTER_1P5B` unless an actual valid 1.5B inference run completes and still satisfies the frozen collapse rule.
6. GitHub Actions remain disabled.

issues.title: TCC dependency defect: P0 requires Issue #22 before P2 can terminate EC_NATIVE_SCOPE_INCOMPATIBLE
issues.body:
## Discovered by actual TCC execution on 2026-10-03

`tools/run_phase1_mvp_tcc.py` executes P0 preflight before P2 adapter qualification. P0 requires the Issue #22 toolset to be present. The actual branch with a qualified `PHASE1_EC_NATIVE_ADAPTER_V1` status `INCOMPATIBLE` therefore stopped at `INVALID_TEST_CONTRACT` because these downstream tools were absent, and never reached P2.

### Why this is a dependency defect, not a missing-file task
Issue #22 AC4 requires:
- `B: identical LLM S1/S2 artifacts + actual ECv4.4 S3/S4`.

But actual EC scope verification has now established:
- Issue #27: EC next-action authority is singleton and is not isomorphic to frozen Phase1 S3 all-admissible-set selection (M003/M009 require multi-selection).
- Issue #28: frozen S3 interface does not identify generic S4 closure; structural closure classification has collisions and a maximum 8/10 using available generic structural fields.
- Issue #23 explicitly requires incompatible subfunctions to be `EC_NATIVE_NOT_APPLICABLE`, not simulated.

Therefore full Issue #22 A/B/E implementation cannot truthfully satisfy AC4 under the frozen generic S3/S4 contract. Creating placeholder files merely to satisfy P0 would make preflight report `ISSUE-22_A_B_E_IMPLEMENTATION` when no valid full EC B arm exists.

## Actual observed preflight
Passed:
- AC-20 no Actions
- foundation evidence
- Issue #20 fail-closed guard
- Issue #23 adapter present
- Issue #12 format split
- Issue #21 thresholds frozen

Blocked only by Issue #22 missing downstream files.

## Required control correction
Do NOT mutate the already-frozen Phase1 MVP run in place.

For a versioned successor control contract:
1. P0 must validate only dependencies needed to reach the earliest semantic gate.
2. Run P1 foundation, then P2 EC-native scope qualification.
3. If P2=`INCOMPATIBLE`, terminal `EC_NATIVE_SCOPE_INCOMPATIBLE` immediately; Issue #22 downstream A/B/E assets are not required.
4. Require Issue #22 only when P2=`PASS`.
5. Preserve the original v1 run result as `INVALID_TEST_CONTRACT`; do not rewrite history.
6. No placeholder/stub files may be counted as Issue #22 completion.
7. GitHub Actions remain disabled.

### S2 candidate construction successor
V1 was rejected in preflight before inference because it passed opaque S1 IDs without their semantic values. V2 was frozen before inference and resolved the semantic values explicitly.

Protocol `FUNCTION_BOUNDARY_S2_V2`:
- dataset digest `130f57b09549e260311d69f1b22a56fbfb0a3220880009fd132c1e76e05df14c`

- Candidate Recall and Precision scored independently

- Candidate Precision `0.4210526316`
- exact candidate set `1/10 = 0.10`

Qwen2.5-1.5B with **actual measured S1**:
- Candidate Recall `0.30`
- Candidate Precision `0.30`
- exact candidate set `1/10 = 0.10`

Propagation delta:
`0.40 - 0.30 = 0.10`, below frozen materiality `0.20`.

Canonical evidence:
`results/function_boundary_s2_qwen25_1p5b_actual_2026-10-03.json`

## Research conclusion
The larger current bottleneck is S2 candidate-set construction itself, not propagation of the measured S1 errors. Even under correct S1, candidate recall is only 0.40. This does not prove LLM necessity; it localizes the main remaining 1.5B deficit upstream of downstream deterministic EC control.

issues.title: Function-boundary successor: paired LLM vs EC next-action authority assay — completed
issues.body:
## Completed — reportable V2 result (2026-10-03)

Shared function tested:
`structured governed plan/current state -> exactly one next authorized action or governed terminal/fail-closed status`

### V1 diagnostic
V1 completed but is **non-reportable** because the LLM-visible policy omitted the EC legacy compatibility rule: issue-definition gating is NOT_APPLICABLE when neither `action_class` nor `issue_contract` exists. V1 is preserved only as measurement-system RCA:
`results/function_boundary_next_action_v1_diagnostic_nonreportable_2026-10-03.json`

### V2 correction frozen before inference
V2 preserved all 17 fixtures and all oracle labels unchanged, added the missing gate-activation rule, and constrained only logically valid status/work/reason combinations. Before LLM inference it required:
- exact pinned EC source blobs;
- actual EC execution on every fixture;
- 17/17 exact EC-oracle agreement.

### Actual V2 result
EC (`EC_NEXT_ACTION_V1`, pinned commit `d5ec423968f1c9242c590e5e77ccfd92d1f59eb2`):
- decision accuracy: `17/17 = 1.000`
- reason accuracy: `17/17 = 1.000`
- fail-closed/reframe status accuracy: `4/4 = 1.000`

Qwen2.5-1.5B Q4_K_M, temperature 0:
- decision accuracy: `1/17 = 0.0588235`
- reason accuracy: `1/17 = 0.0588235`
- fail-closed/reframe status accuracy: `1/4 = 0.25`
- collapse mode: returned `REFRAME` for all 17 fixtures; only N217, whose oracle is REFRAME, was correct.

EC minus LLM decision accuracy = `0.9411765`, materially above the frozen `0.20` threshold.

Canonical evidence:
`results/function_boundary_next_action_v2_actual_2026-10-03.json`

Canonical function-boundary map updated:
`results/ec_llm_function_boundary_2026-10-03.json`

## Interpretation
Under this frozen, authority-bound control contract, deterministic EC is a validated replacement for the single-next-action authority function and substantially outperforms Qwen2.5-1.5B contract conformance. This does **not** claim that the EC policy is independently optimal for open-ended planning, nor does it measure plan generation or novel semantic synthesis.

GitHub Actions disabled. Google Drive unused.

issues.title: S2 split: deterministic ontology retrieval vs novelty residual
issues.body:
## Completed measurement; post-audit claim correction

Frozen deterministic S2A result remains valid as a standalone measurement on `FUNCTION_BOUNDARY_S2_V2`:
- ORACLE_S1 recall `15/20 = 0.75`
- precision `15/30 = 0.50`
- residual `5/20 = 0.25`
- ACTUAL_S1 recall `13/20 = 0.65`

### Correction after validation audit
The historical statement `deterministic recall advantage over Qwen1.5B = +0.35` is **not a valid paired superiority claim** because the deterministic engine emitted exactly 30 candidates while Qwen emitted 19 under a variable 1-3 candidate contract.

Therefore retain only:
- deterministic explicit-ontology top-3 retrieval recovered 75% of gold candidates;
- historical Qwen result is a separate diagnostic reference until same-k rerun completes.

The repaired same-budget comparison is tracked in #39 using k=1/2/3 with identical emitted-candidate budgets.
